Rachel / Karthik — here is a concise commercial proposal we should put in the RFP commercial answers spreadsheet. I kept it conservative to protect unit economics but flexible enough for procurement.

Summary (commercial terms):
- Baseline commit: 10,000,000 tokens/month at $0.00080 per token (monthly invoice).
- Overage rate: $0.00120 per token above committed volume, billed monthly.
- Monthly Burst Credit Pool: 15% of monthly commit (1,500,000 tokens) allocated as a "burst cushion". Consumption of burst cushion is charged at $0.00095 per token (i.e., 18.75% premium to commit rate, lower than overage). The burst pool auto-reset monthly.
- Convertible Quarterly True-up: Unused committed tokens may be converted to refundable credits on a quarterly true-up (rolling), usable for subsequent months within the same 12-month contract year. Credits expire at contract year-end unless an annual true-up is executed.
- Multi-year discount: 10% discount on per-token rates for a 24-month committed term (applies to baseline commit only).
- Minimum annual commitment: equivalent of 6x monthly baseline for new logos; standard for enterprise is 12x for renewal/expansion deals.
- SLA service credits: credits applied as a percentage reduction to the monthly invoice. Example: if 99.5% latency SLO missed for >3 days in month, 5% invoice credit; if missed >7 days, 15% credit (capped at 30% of invoice). Credits never exceed the monthly service fee.

Notes on rationale:
- Burst pool priced between commit and raw overage to incentivize reasonable provisioned commit while protecting app spikes.
- Quarterly true-up reduces month-to-month churn while giving procurement flexibility.
- SLA credits as invoice percent are easier operationally (no token re-injection bookkeeping).

I'll attach a sample line-item that you can paste into ContainWell's commercial sheet.

Attachments: ContainWell-RFP-commercial-answers-v1.xlsx (draft line-items).

Ben Carter
Director, Commercial Strategy

Hi Alice — thanks for the questions and for the annotated sheet. Per internal review, please find our commercial responses below (I also attached the populated commercial answers spreadsheet and our SLA latency targets doc):

1) Burst capacity pricing: We propose a separate monthly Burst Credit Pool equal to 15% of your committed monthly token volume. Consumption of the burst pool is billed at $0.00095 per token (midpoint between commit and overage) and resets monthly. Pure overage beyond commit + burst pool is billed at $0.00120 per token. This structure keeps spikes cheaper than raw overage while encouraging a sensible commit.

2) Rollover / credits: We will do quarterly true-ups. Unused committed tokens at quarter end can be converted to credits usable in later months within the same 12-month contract year. At the annual true-up, customers may request conversion to a one-time refund or apply credits to a renew/upgrade if the account is in good standing. Additionally, as an optional term for ContainWell, we can include a Reserve Cushion equal to up to 5% of annual committed tokens that can be reserved for seasonality; those tokens are refundable or convertible at the annual true-up.

3) SLA credits: Service credits tied to missed latency SLOs are applied as percentage reductions to the monthly invoice. Proposed examples (for the RFP):
   - Miss 99.5% latency target for >3 days in the month: 5% credit to monthly invoice
   - Miss for >7 days: 15% credit
   - Capped at 30% of the monthly invoice (legal standard cap)

Commercial highlights:
- Baseline commit: 10,000,000 tokens/month @ $0.00080/token
- Burst credit pool: 15% of commit @ $0.00095/token (resets monthly)
- Overage: $0.00120/token after commit + burst use
- Quarterly true-up; annual true-up supports refund/conversion of credits
- 24-month term = 10% off per-token baseline rates; early termination carve-outs to be negotiated
- Minimum annual commitment and early-termination terms included in the attached worksheet

Attachments: ContainWell-RFP-commercial-answers-v1.xlsx; SLA_latency_targets.pdf

If ContainWell prefers month-to-month rollover instead of quarterly, we can show an alternative pricing schedule (with smaller discount) — let me know which you prefer and I will produce a short addendum.

Thanks again — happy to hop on 30 minutes with your team if that helps.
